html:
The Tepehuán are an Indigenous people of the Sierra Madre Occidental in northwestern Mexico, mostly in Durango, Chihuahua and Nayarit. Their language, in three branches, is closely related to O'odham, spoken far to the north by the Pima.

They farmed maize and beans in mountain valleys and hunted. Spanish silver mines and Jesuit missions spread into their land from the late 1500s. In 1616 the Tepehuán rose in the Tepehuán Revolt, killing Jesuit missionaries and settlers; the Spanish took years to crush it.

Neighbours include the Rarámuri, the Wixárika, the Xixime and the Acaxee. See also Tepehuane.
